case_title: Jasdeep Singh @ Jassu v. State of Punjab
accused_socioeconomic_status: Not stated by the Court. Complainant's counsel alleged the accused are influential persons; no finding made.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute: alleged that the deceased believed the accused instigated a raid on the family hotel. No other relationship stated.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304 Part I; IPC s.34
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW6, PW10); recovery of weapons; medical evidence; statement attributed to accused; PW13 testimony on prior plan (disbelieved); dying declaration (rejected)
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden fight in heat of passion; no premeditation (trial court finding); deceased went nearer to the accused rather than the accused waiting for him.
trial_court_outcome: All four accused convicted under s.304 Part I IPC with life sentence
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; trial court's conviction under s.304 Part I upheld. High Court did not specifically consider s.34 as against A3 and A4.
neutral_facts: At about 12:45 a.m. on 21 April 2011, the victim was shot dead on a street in Jalandhar. The prosecution case was that the victim believed a raid on a hotel run by his family had been instigated by the accused, and that a quarrel preceded the incident. A witness who went looking for the victim saw the accused grappling with him under a street light. A friend of the victim was also present; this witness later turned hostile at trial. The prosecution alleged that, shortly before the shooting, two of the accused made the remark 'what are you seeing now', after which another accused, who had already drawn a gun and brandished it at the victim, took out a gun from his pocket and fired a single shot. The victim was taken to a hospital about three kilometres away in a car, and a complaint was lodged. The investigating officer completed the investigation and recovered weapons. Medical evidence was on record. A further witness claimed to have overheard a prior plan to commit the murder, but this account was contested. The defence examined its own witnesses. The evidence on the fight and the sequence of events was disputed in its details, including the supplementary statement attributed to the victim's father.
physical_harm: Death of the deceased from a single gunshot
number_of_offences: 1 charged (s.304 Part I IPC, with s.34 IPC as liability provision); 0 finally upheld against A3 and A4
premeditation_planning: No premeditation found by the trial court; Supreme Court held the findings did not suffer from perversity. Prior-concert evidence of PW13 disbelieved.
motive: alleged: deceased believed the accused had instigated a raid on the family hotel
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of PW6 not rejected, though exaggerated; findings that the deceased went nearer to the accused and that the single shot was fired by A1 were not disturbed. The 'what are you seeing now' statement was the only material against A3 and A4 and was held insufficient.
witness_credibility: PW13 disbelieved (improbabilities; contradicted by cousin DW1). PW6 exaggerated and made concerted efforts to improve the case. PW10 turned hostile; his prior statement was considered by the trial court.
trial_duration: offence: 21.04.2011; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 16.10.2019; Supreme Court: January 07, 2022
legal_representation: Appellants (A3, A4): Shekhar Naphade, Siddharth Luthra, Vikram Chaudhri (Sr. Advs.) and others listed in cause title, not allocated individually. State: counsel not named. Complainant: Senior Counsel (not named).
investigation_status: Investigation completed by PW24; recoveries including weapons made. Charge sheet date not stated.
procedural_irregularity: High Court did not consider the scope of s.34 IPC as against A3 and A4
appeal_history: Trial court: all four convicted under s.304 Part I IPC with life sentence. High Court: appeals dismissed, conviction upheld. Supreme Court: A3 and A4 appeals allowed (acquitted); complainant's appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Complainant's counsel: accused are influential; case falls under s.302 IPC; trial court erred in applying s.304 Part I; physical act not necessary under s.34. State: High Court reasoning cogent; recoveries proved; no interference needed.
defence_argument: PW13's evidence disbelieved so s.34 wrongly applied; PW6's account improved; presence of PW6 doubtful; if A2 had brandished the gun, A3 and A4 would have asked A2 to shoot; PW10 and PW23 turned hostile.
legal_principle_applied: Section 34 IPC requires proof of common intention and participation/act in furtherance; prosecution bears the onus; where part of evidence is disbelieved, remaining evidence must be examined with care; mere presence insufficient without evidence of common intention.
precedent_relied_upon: Suresh v State of U.P. (2001) 3 SCC 673; Lallan Rai v. State of Bihar (2003) 1 SCC 268; Chhota Ahirwar v. State of M.P. (2020) 4 SCC 126; Rambilas Singh v. State of Bihar (1989) 3 SCC 605; Krishnan v. State of Kerala (1996) 10 SCC 508; Surendra Chauhan v. State of M.P. (2000) 4 SCC 110; Gopi Nath v. State of U.P. (2001) 6 SCC 620; Ramesh Singh v. State of A.P. (2004) 11 SCC 305; Nand Kishore v. State of M.P. (2011) 12 SCC 120; Shyamal Ghosh v. State of West Bengal (2012) 7 SCC 646; Virendra Singh v. State of M.P. (2010) 8 SCC 407. Referred: Barendra Kumar Ghosh (AIR 1925 PC 1); Shah v. Emperor (AIR 1945 PC 148).
